findings.title: Observing one project deletes every other project's polling state
findings.description:
`RunnerTenant` shares one `RunObserver` across all projects, but each `ProjectTick` supplies only its own entries. These cleanup operations therefore discard `_last_poll`, `_overdue`, and `_faulted` records belonging to other projects.

With two projects visited on each tick, confirmed runs can be polled every tick instead of respecting `run_poll_interval_seconds`. Standing faults and overdue-launch state are also lost between visits. Scope observer state and cleanup by project, or give each project its own observer. Add a multi-project regression test covering polling cadence and fault persistence.

findings.title: The launch budget is checked before potentially blocking journal work
findings.description:
The budget check in `_act` occurs before `_launch` validates arguments and commits `journal_issue`. The SQLite write can wait for contention or durable storage, allowing the deadline to expire—or a stop request to arrive—before `launch` starts `Popen`. Neither `_launch` nor `launch` checks the budget again.

This violates the stated guarantee that no subprocess starts after the deadline or a stop request. Recheck immediately before spawning and explicitly handle an entry that was journaled but not launched. Add a regression test where journal issuance advances the clock past the deadline or requests shutdown.

findings.title: Unconfirmed launches do not replay standing poll failures
findings.description:
When an unconfirmed launch receives a `PollFailure`, `_fault` saves it in `_faulted`. On the next tick before another poll is due, this branch calls `_still_overdue`, which does not replay that saved observation fault.

Consequently, `ProjectTick._close_recovered` can close the `run_observation_failed` escalation even though no successful observation has occurred. Persistent failures can repeatedly open and close escalations at the polling cadence. Replay standing poll faults for unconfirmed launches, as `_confirmed` already does, and test consecutive ticks with fresh `TickFaults` instances.
